finding: Calibrated to Apr 2025, BG/NBD predicted 38 repeat orders from existing buyers in May–Oct 2025 vs 47 actual (-20%). Ranking who will buy: AUC 0.45 (recency alone 0.47, frequency alone 0.43). No individual signal: neither the model nor recency or frequency can tell who will buy next. The customer-base simulation (03) forecast aggregate orders better (-1%).

Repeat orders per buyer match a single shared Poisson rate of 3.6%/month (dispersion 1.03, p=0.37). BG/NBD agrees: its fitted parameters collapse to one rate with no drop-out. Buyers do not differ in how often they buy, and nobody measurably 'churns': every buyer is equally likely to order next month.

Average P(order in next 90 days) 10% (range 10%–11%). Expected orders from all 216 buyers in the next 90 days ≈ 23. P(alive) is ~100% for everyone. Scores are near-identical, so **do not build propensity-based targeting** on this data: give every buyer the same follow-up cadence.

Expected gross profit from existing buyers over the next 12 months ≈ ₹69.7 L (median ₹31,897 per buyer, top ₹37,579). Top 20% of buyers hold only 21% of it: future value is spread almost evenly, and individual differences come only from past order value, heavily shrunk. The total is the useful number (cross-check: 216 buyers x 3.6%/month x 12 x avg profit/order). Frequency vs order-value correlation 0.09 (independent, so Gamma-Gamma is valid). No discounting applied over 12 months.

38 repeat buyers are silent for 2x+ their own usual gap (historical run-rate ≈ ₹41.0 L/yr). But the rule does not predict: applied at Apr 2025, flagged buyers ordered in the next 6 months at 11% vs 18% for others (p=0.53). Long silence is normal for a ~4%/month buyer, not a churn signal. Use output/churn_risk_customers.csv as a re-engagement contact list, not as a risk prediction.

Last 12 months re-priced with item discounts capped at 10% and no stacking: gross profit +₹12.2 L (+12.8%) if volume holds, +9.2% if affected orders fall 10%. It only stops paying off if 36% of affected volume is lost. EDA Q28 found discounts do not drive repeat buying, so a large loss is unlikely.

16 of 80 never-ordered customers converting adds ≈ ₹10.8 L from first orders (avg first-order profit ₹67,772) plus ≈ ₹5.2 L from their repeat orders in the following 12 months (0.43 expected repeats each): ≈ ₹16.0 L in total, about 17% of the 2026 base forecast.

Raising the repeat rate from 53% to 60% means 16 more of today's one-time buyers ordering again. At ₹72,924 profit per order that adds ≈ ₹11.7 L of profit. But PPAC would move from ₹92,247 to ≈ ₹89,693: it FALLS, because each re-activated buyer adds one average order but a whole extra 'active customer'. PPAC rewards deepening existing relationships, not widening them; track it alongside total gross profit and repeat rate.
